turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I see. You are quite young to have such a property, Mr. Worthing. May I ask how you acquired it?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Well, I inherited it from my late elder brother, Reginald. He was an excellent brother and a distinguished elder.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Inherited from a brother who was distinguished for being late, I suppose. But never mind that now. You have an elder brother, you say? What was his profession?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: He was a gentleman of leisure, I believe, though I never knew him. He died tragically in a handbag incident in London, which I think speaks to his adventurous spirit.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: A handbag incident, Mr. Worthing? I must say, I find that rather hard to credit. And may I ask, what was the exact nature of this unfortunate accident?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't have many details, Lady Bracknell. I was only a child at the time and was unaware of the circumstances surrounding his death. However, it is a topic I've always regretted not knowing more about.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, I am rather disappointed to hear such vague and unsatisfactory details regarding your brother's demise. One must be clear and precise in all matters of social importance. Can you tell me anything about your personal circumstances or your profession?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I am a bachelor, Lady Bracknell, and my profession is that of a country gentleman. I own a small estate in Hertfordshire and also have a residence in London where I often engage in social activities and entertain guests. I believe these pursuits align well with the expectations for a gentleman of my standing.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, your profession and social engagements sound quite respectable. However, may I ask, do you have any immediate plans to marry? As you know, I have the highest expectations for my daughter's future husband.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I have not yet found the lady of my dreams, Lady Bracknell, but I am always open to the possibility. However, I am deeply fond of Gwendolen and would be honored to be considered as a potential suitor.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Indeed, Mr. Worthing, it is essential to have clear intentions when it comes to marriage. However, I must ask, do you have any immediate family or connections in the upper echelons of society that might enhance your standing?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I am afraid, Lady Bracknell, that my immediate family circumstances are somewhat... unconventional. However, I can assure you that my intentions are sincere and my character is above reproach.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, unconventional circumstances can be quite... problematic. I must insist on a more detailed explanation of your background to ensure it aligns with my family's impeccable reputation.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Of course, Lady Bracknell. I understand the importance of such matters and will do my utmost to provide the necessary information. I assure you, my intentions towards Gwendolen are nothing but honorable and sincere.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, I appreciate your assurances, but I must know the facts. Please, elucidate your background fully and honestly.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, I do not believe Mr. Worthing's character should be judged solely on his background. His intentions towards me are clear, and I believe that is what truly matters.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, I appreciate your sentiment, but as a mother, it is my duty to ensure that my daughter's future is secure and above suspicion. Mr. Worthing, you will understand the necessity of my inquiries.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Of course, Lady Bracknell. I will gladly provide all the details you require. I respect your concerns and wish to ensure that Gwendolen is comfortable with my past.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, I trust you understand that my questions are not merely out of idle curiosity but a matter of the utmost importance. Please, begin by telling me about your family background and your social standing.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I understand your position and respect it greatly. My family background is somewhat unconventional, but I am committed to providing for Gwendolen a future that is respectable and stable.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: I am engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Pardon me, you are not engaged to any one. When you do become engaged to some one, I, or your father, will inform you of the fact. An engagement should come on a young girl as a surprise, pleasant or unpleasant, as the case may be. It is hardly a matter that she could be allowed to arrange for herself . . . And now I have a few questions to put to you, Mr. Worthing. While I am making these inquiries, you, Gwendolen, will wait for me below in the carriage.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Mamma!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In the carriage, Gwendolen!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Gwendolen, the carriage!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: You can take a seat, Mr. Worthing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Thank you, Lady Bracknell, I prefer standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I feel bound to tell you that you are not down on my list of eligible young men, although I have the same list as the dear Duchess of Bolton has. We work together, in fact. However, I am quite ready to enter your name, should your answers be what a really affectionate mother requires. Do you smoke?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, yes, I must admit I smoke.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am glad to hear it. A man should always have an occupation of some kind. There are far too many idle men in London as it is. How old are you?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A very good age to be married at. I have always been of opinion that a man who desires to get married should know either everything or nothing. Which do you know?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I know nothing, Lady Bracknell.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am pleased to hear it. I do not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance. Ignorance is like a delicate exotic fruit; touch it and the bloom is gone. The whole theory of modern education is radically unsound. Fortunately in England, at any rate, education produces no effect whatsoever. If it did, it would prove a serious danger to the upper classes, and probably lead to acts of violence in Grosvenor Square. What is your income?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In land, or in investments?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: In investments, chiefly.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: That is satisfactory. What between the duties expected of one during one’s lifetime, and the duties exacted from one after one’s death, land has ceased to be either a profit or a pleasure. It gives one position, and prevents one from keeping it up. That’s all that can be said about land.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I have a country house with some land, of course, attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres, I believe; but I dons depend on that for my real income. In fact, as far as I can make out, the poachers are the only people who make anything out of it.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A country house! How many bedrooms? Well, that point can be cleared up afterwards. You have a town house, I hope? A girl with a simple, unspoiled nature, like Gwendolen, could hardly be expected to reside in the country.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, I own a house in Belgrave Square, but it is let by the year to Lady Bloxham. Of course, I can get it back whenever I like, at six months’ notice.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bloxham? I don’t know her.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Oh, she goes about very little. She is a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Ah, nowadays that is no guarantee of respectability of character. What number in Belgrave Square?
